notes: Every number below comes from a published source listed under 'sources'. Where sources disagree we keep one internally consistent primary source (WRAP 2012 for fibres) and record the range in 'note'.

Carbon factors for fibres are WRAP's whole-life-cycle footprint per kg of fibre in UK clothing (production is ~3/4 of it, laundry ~1/4). They are NOT strictly cradle-to-gate; use them for relative comparison between materials.
Water factors are WRAP's water footprint per kg of fibre (m3 per tonne == litres per kg). WRAP notes there is little data on water use for synthetic fibres.
Where no sourced number exists the entry says so and either uses the closest sourced material ('proxy_for') or is null (not estimated).

wrap_2012_voc.title: Valuing our clothes: the true cost of how we design, use and dispose of clothing in the UK (Table 1, Table 3 'Variations in footprint by fibre type', Table 4 'using clothes for longer')

ethical_consumer_2024.title: What is the carbon cost of clothing? (table 'CO2 equivalent produced per kg fabric', attributed to WRAP 2012)

nordic_2014.title: Changing consumer behaviour towards increased prevention of textile waste - Background report (Table 3), R. Nielsen & A. Schmidt, FORCE Technology, NA2014:927

te_2014_organic_cotton.title: The Life Cycle Assessment of Organic Cotton Fiber - A Global Average (conducted by PE International)

carbonfact_polyester.title: The Carbon Footprint of Polyester (fossil PET 3.12 kg CO2e/kg; mechanically recycled PET 0.68-1.56 kg CO2e/kg, ecoinvent-based)

foen_2017_recycled.title: Recycled Textile Fibres and Textile Recycling (cites ~32% lower CO2 for recycled vs virgin polyester fibre)
foen_2017_recycled.publisher: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN)

astudillo_2015_silk.title: Life cycle assessment of silk production - a case study from India (Astudillo, Thalwitz & Vollrath), Handbook of LCA of Textiles and Clothing pp. 255-274; values as tabulated in Material Innovation Initiative 'What makes silk, silk?' press release

brugnoli_2025_leather.title: A global study on the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of the modern cow leather industry (Brugnoli et al., Discover Sustainability 6:80), 22.0 kg CO2e per kg leather; range reported alongside Roncevich et al. 2026 (187.1 kg CO2e/kg) and LWG 2024 (22.48 kg CO2e per m2)
brugnoli_2025_leather.publisher: Discover Sustainability (Springer); summarised by US Leather / Institute for Data Integrity (industry-affiliated)

lwg_2024_leather.title: Measuring the Environmental Impact of Leather: Life Cycle Assessment - summary (22.48 kg CO2e per m2 finished leather; 68% from farming & slaughter)

cheah_2013_shoes.title: Manufacturing-focused emissions reductions in footwear production (Cheah, Kirchain et al., J. Cleaner Production 44:18-29) - synthetic running shoe 14 +/- 2.7 kg CO2e per pair, cradle-to-grave

bodoga_2024_boots.title: Environmental Impact of Footwear Using Life Cycle Assessment - Case Study of Professional Footwear (Bodoga et al., Sustainability 16(14):6094) - leather safety boots 18.65 kg CO2e per pair, cradle-to-grave; cites GORE-TEX hiking boot LCA at 27.1 kg CO2e per pair

pefcr_af_2021.title: Draft Product Environmental Footprint Category Rules (PEFCR) Apparel and Footwear, v1.1 second draft (28 May 2021), Table 6 'Default product duration of service per product sub-category' (number of wears; 1 use = 1 day of wear)
pefcr_af_2021.publisher: EU PEF pilot / Sustainable Apparel Coalition technical secretariat (hosted by EEB)

ecobalyse.title: Ecobalyse textile environmental-cost tool (French Ministry of Ecological Transition / ADEME): products.json (daysOfWear per product, matches PEFCR Table 6) and examples.json (example product masses)

sandin_2019.title: Environmental assessment of Swedish clothing consumption - six garments, sustainable futures (Sandin, Roos, Spak, Zamani, Peters), Table 3.1 masses and Table 3.6 number of uses

cottoninc_2019.title: Changes in Average Garment Weight & End-Use Demand (J. Devine), Table 1 average product weight from import data

wrap_2014_longevity.title: Clothing Longevity Protocol (Cooper et al., Nottingham Trent University for WRAP), Figure 2: current lifetime (years) and average wear days per year

emf_2017.title: A New Textiles Economy: Redesigning fashion's future - summary of findings (clothing utilisation down 36% in 15 years; in the US clothes are worn around a quarter of the global average)

quantis_2018.title: Measuring Fashion: Environmental Impact of the Global Apparel and Footwear Industries Study (fibre production ~15% of apparel GHG; dyeing & finishing 36%, yarn preparation 28%)

laitala_2018.title: Does Use Matter? Comparison of Environmental Impacts of Clothing Based on Fiber Type (Laitala, Klepp & Henry), Sustainability 10(7):2524

cotton.note: WRAP 2012 Table 3. Range: Nordic 2014 uses 13.9 kg CO2e/kg and 5,597 L/kg (green+blue) for cotton (PE International data). Denim and most jersey/twill/pique/poplin/corduroy fabrics map here.

organic_cotton.note: Derived: WRAP cotton minus the fibre-stage difference reported by Textile Exchange 2014: GWP 1,808 -> 978 kg CO2e per t fibre (-0.83 kg/kg), blue water 2,120 -> 182 m3 per t fibre (-1,938 L/kg). Textile Exchange warns the comparison is indicative (two separate studies).

polyester.note: WRAP 2012 Table 3. Range: Nordic 2014 16.9 kg CO2e/kg, 78 L/kg. Fossil-based and sheds microfibres (Laitala 2018) - not captured in CO2e. Satin, fleece, chiffon, 'synthetic' map here.

recycled_polyester.note: Derived: WRAP polyester (21) minus fibre-stage saving: fossil PET 3.12 vs mechanically recycled PET 0.68-1.56 (midpoint 1.12) kg CO2e/kg -> -2.0 kg/kg. FOEN 2017 cites ~32% lower CO2 at fibre level; only the fibre stage (~15% of apparel GHG, Quantis 2018) changes, so the whole-life saving is ~10%. Water: no sourced difference, kept equal to polyester.

nylon.note: WRAP 2012 Table 3 'Polyamide (nylon)'. Range: Nordic 2014 20.2 kg CO2e/kg, 78 L/kg.

acrylic.note: WRAP 2012 Table 3. Range: Nordic 2014 35.4 kg CO2e/kg, 128 L/kg.

wool.note: WRAP 2012 Table 3. Range: Nordic 2014 44.4 kg CO2e/kg, 16,379 L/kg (green+blue). Cashmere, merino, alpaca, mohair, tweed map here (no separate sourced factor).

viscose.note: WRAP 2012 Table 3. Range: Nordic 2014 26.4 kg CO2e/kg, 3,829 L/kg. Rayon, modal, lyocell/Tencel, bamboo viscose map here (lyocell is usually lower; no separate sourced factor used).

linen.note: 'Flax linen' 15 kg CO2e/kg in the WRAP 2012 figures reproduced by Ethical Consumer 2024. Water: no litres-per-kg figure on the same basis found (European flax is mostly rain-fed; the CELC LCA reports a scarcity-weighted metric, not litres), so water is not estimated. Hemp maps here as the closest sourced bast fibre.

silk.note: 25 kg CO2e/kg in the WRAP 2012 figures reproduced by Ethical Consumer 2024. Range: Astudillo et al. 2015 raw silk (India) 51.5 kg CO2e/kg. Water is Astudillo's BLUE water footprint 24.6 m3/kg of raw silk (different basis from WRAP; other studies range from ~445 L/kg handwoven to >25,000 L/kg).

polyurethane.note: 'Polyurethane' 20 kg CO2e/kg in the WRAP 2012 figures reproduced by Ethical Consumer 2024. Elastane/spandex/Lycra is ~85% segmented polyurethane (Laitala 2018 Table 1) so it maps here, as do PU / faux / vegan leather. Water: no sourced figure; uses polyester's 80 L/kg as the closest sourced synthetic.

leather.note: Brugnoli et al. 2025: 22.0 kg CO2e per kg (industry primary data, cradle-to-gate). Highly allocation-dependent: Roncevich et al. 2026 report 187.1 kg CO2e/kg; LWG 2024 22.48 kg CO2e per m2. We use the primary-data value and flag the range. Water not estimated. Not used for shoes (shoes use per-pair footprints). Suede maps here.

unknown.note: Fallback 'average textile'. Derived from WRAP 2012 totals: 38 Mt CO2e and 6,300 million m3 water per year for UK clothing / 1.76 Mt raw materials used. Cross-check: Nordic 2014 'average textile' = 21 kg CO2e/kg and 4,527 L/kg. Also used as the reference fibre for the score (score 50 = a typical garment of the same type in an average textile).

tshirt.note: Ecobalyse example T-shirt 150 g; Cotton Inc 2019 US import average 0.16 kg; Sandin 2019 example 110 g. PEFCR 'T-shirts' 45 wears (Sandin 2019: 30; WRAP 2014: 3.3 yr x 25 wear-days = ~82). Tanks, camis, polos and generic tops map here (tanks/camis likely lighter).

shirt.note: Ecobalyse example shirt ('chemise') 250 g. PEFCR 'Shirts and blouses' 40 wears (WRAP 2014: 3.6 yr x 16 = ~58).

sweater.note: Ecobalyse example sweater ('pull') 550 g. PEFCR 'Sweaters and midlayers' 85 wears (WRAP 2014 knitwear: 3.7 yr x 30 = ~111). Hoodies, sweatshirts, cardigans, fleeces map here.

trousers.note: Ecobalyse example trousers ('pantalon') 450 g; Cotton Inc 2019 woven cotton bottoms 0.49 kg (men) / 0.38 kg (women). PEFCR 'Pants and shorts' 70 wears. Chinos, slacks, leggings, joggers map here.

jeans.note: Ecobalyse example jeans 450 g; Sandin 2019 example 477 g; Carlsson 2011 (via Sandin) typical 700 g. PEFCR 'Pants and shorts' 70 wears (Sandin 2019: 240; WRAP 2014: 3.1 yr x 75 = ~232).

shorts.note: No separate sourced weight: Ecobalyse's 'Pantalon / Short' category (450 g example) and Cotton Inc's HS 620342/620462 both lump shorts with trousers, so shorts are probably over-estimated. PEFCR 'Pants and shorts' 70 wears.

skirt.note: Ecobalyse example skirt/dress ('jupe / robe') 300 g. PEFCR 'Dresses, skirts and jumpsuits' 70 wears.

dress.note: Ecobalyse example 'jupe / robe' 300 g; Sandin 2019 lined polyester dress 478 g. PEFCR 'Dresses, skirts and jumpsuits' 70 wears (Sandin 2019: 26 uses in Sweden). Jumpsuits map here.

jacket.note: Sandin 2019 example jacket 444 g (Ecobalyse lumps coats and jackets at 950 g). PEFCR 'Jackets and coats' 100 wears (Sandin 2019: 140, an unsupported assumption per the authors). Blazers, bombers, denim jackets, vests map here.

coat.note: Ecobalyse example coat ('manteau / veste') 950 g. PEFCR 'Jackets and coats' 100 wears. Parkas, puffers, trench coats, overcoats map here.

sneakers.note: Cheah et al. 2013 synthetic running shoe 14 +/- 2.7 kg CO2e/pair (PUMA 2008 / Timberland 2009 reported 18-41). PEFCR 'Closed-toed shoes' 100 wears. Loafers, heels, flats, oxfords also map here (closest sourced product). Water not estimated.

boots.note: Bodoga et al. 2024 leather safety boots 18.65 kg CO2e/pair (range: GORE-TEX hiking boots 27.1). PEFCR 'Boots' 100 wears. Water not estimated.

sandals.note: No sourced per-pair figure for sandals; uses the running-shoe value as the closest sourced product (probably an over-estimate). PEFCR 'Open-toed shoes' 50 wears. Water not estimated.

life_extension_evidence.value: +33% active life (9 months) -> -27% carbon, -33% water, -22% waste; +10% (3 months) -> -8% carbon, -10% water
life_extension_evidence.note: WRAP 2012 Table 4. Consistent with footprint-per-wear scaling as 1/wears (+33% wears -> -25% per wear).

utilisation_spread_evidence.value: US clothes are worn ~1/4 as often as the global average; global utilisation fell 36% in 15 years
utilisation_spread_evidence.note: Used only to bound the (assumed) utility multiplier to a 4x spread: 0.5x .. 2.0x of the baseline wears.
